statement: You are given an array nums sorted in non-decreasing order (it may contain duplicates) and an integer target.

The lower bound of target is the smallest index i such that nums[i] ≥ target. When the array contains target, this is the index of its first copy; when it does not, it is the position where target would have to be inserted to keep the array sorted.
Return the lower bound. If every element is smaller than target, no such index exists and the answer is n, the length of the array. Use binary search, so the work is O(log n).

examples.explanation: nums[1] = 2 is the first element that is at least 2. Indices 2 and 3 also hold 2, but index 1 is the smallest.
6 is not in the array. nums[3] = 7 is the first element that is not below 6, so the lower bound is 3.
